properties.Please provide a short description of yo: A place for beginner crafters and experienced designers to create memorable works in a variety of mediums. We provide the classes, tools, and space to inspire your passion projects. We offer quarterly studio passes, 6-week classes, and one-day workshops.
properties.Is your space affiliated with a college: No, we are an extracurricular program through ASI
properties.Who is allowed to access and use your sp: Active Cal Poly students, faculty and staff. However, we do not currently have walk-ins for most of our studio spaces; you must register on a quarter-to-quarter basis.
properties.If you hours are stated clearly on your: This academic year, our hours are M-F 10am-8pm, and Sat/Sun 10am-6pm, although these hours will be changing/expanding with semester conversion.
properties.What service(s) do you provide? Select a: Repair or Maintenance (bike, surfboard, etc);Studios in sewing, ceramics, glass, and surfboard shaping. Classes/workshops in all of the above, plus jewelry making, leatherworking, painting, stamp making, cyanotype.;
properties.How is the use of your space or services: students pay per class or workshop
properties.If you have a required training, What is: Depends - studio passes require a safety orientation training renewed on an annual basis. Craft Center Coordinator reaches out after successful registration. Currently offered weeks 2 of the quarter, although this will change in semesters.
properties.Does 'Maker space' accurately describe t: We are less drop-in than other makerspaces, and we don't have a lot of the disciplines others have (woodworking, electronics, 3D printers, etc)... It's really more of a crafting community space, but we have some overlap. We operate on a per-term basis (for now, quarters, and later, semesters) and currently don't function offering daily passes or drop-ins to use tools unless registered for the quarter.

properties.Please provide a short description of yo: The CAED Support Shop includes various tools and equipment in support of class and lab activities within the CAED. These include but are not limited to: wood-shop, sheetmetal shop, metal fabrication areas, bronze and aluminum foundry, manual machine tools, CNC plasma cutter and routers, as well as various hand tools.
properties.Who is allowed to access and use your sp: Students currently enrolled in courses in the CAED
properties.What service(s) do you provide? Select a: Wood Shop or Machine Shop;see above;
properties.How is the use of your space or services: free, but students must provide their own materials
properties.If you have a required training, What is:
We have three separate safety training modules the first in the series is in the wood-shop. We also have a metal shop module and a welding module.
Each module consists of hand-on, scripted training for each tool or piece of equipment and a written test and signed user agreement.
Training is typically scheduled/coordinated with faculty or faculty advisors within classes and or groups.
properties.Does 'Maker space' accurately describe t:
Editorial answer....I think the term "Maker space" has, to some degree, become synonymous with spaces dedicated to processes like 3D printing and laser cutting etc. The CAED Support Shop is a shop space that has multiple equipment/tools that fall well outside of that general vernacular. ie: wood-shop, metal fabrication, foundry, manual and CNC tools etc.
I think our name CAED Support Shop is the best descriptor we have come up with thus far.

properties.Does 'Maker space' accurately describe t:
Yes, I also typically see it written Makerspace. 
I’d be interested to see how broadly you define “Makerspace” in terms of the types of shop spaces included. There are many shops on campus with varying levels of access and focus. Some have strict access requirements, while others are more open; some are broad in scope, and others are highly specialized.

For example, the art shops are excellent general resources, but access is limited to students enrolled in art courses. There are also spaces like the Rose Float shop that have a wide range of tools but are centered around a singular specific goal. The Shakespeare press is open to everyone but only does printing. In contrast, senior project labs and research spaces often house highly specialized equipment tailored to particular projects or materials. 

I’m looking forward to seeing how you approach this.

properties.Please provide a short description of yo: Cal Poly College of Engineering Student Machine Shops is a collaborative and safety-conscious learning environment where students complete the cycle of design, from concept to finished product. The machine shops’ primary interest has been to expand the creative potential of Cal Poly students. From basic hand and power tools to state-of-the-art computer controlled machines, students are exposed to the myriad of processes and technologies that comprise today’s’ manufacturing and fabricating environment in a step-by-step manner. Our shops' goal is to break down barriers; where students might have once saw tools and machines as intimidating or disconnected from their own experience, they are now empowered. Both Mustang 60 and the Hangar are open to any students enrolled at Cal Poly!

properties.How is the use of your space or services: Free, students must provide their own materials but we do have some free materials/scraps available for students to use!
properties.Is there a mandatory class or training t: Yes, students must take a red-tag or blue-tag certification (CENG Machine Shop/CAED Support Shop)
